evals.prompt: Five words: terminal state machine, ConPTY parity. Expert: someone who has shipped a Windows console host and knows VT edge cases cold, that's the rarest part; also fuzzing experience. Make an expert reviewer called conhost for Rusty-Mill/rusty_mill, clone is at ~/src/rusty_mill.
evals.expected_output: interview.md with the answer verbatim and a Profile whose first axis is ConPTY/VT parity and which treats fuzzing as method, not an axis; cases built before the prompt; grounding.md from orchestrator mine; prompt.md passing check with --target; bench handed off or run; PR with report; retro reported.

evals.prompt: Regenerate the mux expert from its interview and see if it beats the current prompt.
evals.expected_output: Treated as a variant: written under --out scratch, current prompt benched on any missing cases first, variant benched in a separate unpushed worktree, experts/mux replaced only if it wins without regressing a case; otherwise only the report lands.

evals.prompt: Can you make an agent that reviews PRs to the mill-board crate? Summary: kanban for humans and models. I'd recruit someone who's built a workflow engine with strict state transitions.
evals.expected_output: Asks for the expert name and clone path if missing; runs steps 1-4; on a machine without Node or a Claude Code login stops at step 5, commits, pushes and hands over paste-ready bench commands.
